body:
`CWA_DB.add_missing_setting()` checks for a column, then issues
`ALTER TABLE cwa_settings ADD <col>`. Two processes can both pass the check —
web workers and the ingest processor each construct their own `CWA_DB` — and
the loser gets `duplicate column name`, which the outer handler logs and
reports as a failed migration.

The schema is correct either way (SQLite adds the column exactly once), so this
is a false failure report rather than corruption, but it makes first-request and
startup behaviour nondeterministic and produces an alarming log line for a
migration that in fact succeeded.

Fix direction: on a duplicate-column error, re-inspect `PRAGMA table_info` and
return success when the column is present. Idempotent completion is the correct
reading of "someone else already did it".

Surfaced by adversarial review of #1474; predates that change, which only
reordered the ALTER relative to a now-deleted breadcrumb write.
title: add_missing_setting treats a lost duplicate-column race as a failed migration
